What if humans could breathe underwater?
Fish get oxygen with gills. But water holds about thirty times less oxygen than air.
And water is about eight hundred times denser than air, so pumping it in and out of our lungs would be exhausting.
That's why fish don't breathe in and out. Water flows one way, straight across their gills.
Scientists have tested liquid breathing with oxygen-rich liquids called perfluorocarbons. Mice have survived breathing them.
Doctors have even trialled it to help premature babies with damaged lungs.
But to live in the sea, we'd still face the cold and the pressure. Every ten metres down adds the weight of another whole atmosphere.
